This is a re-check by a non-author of the copd-exacerbation reply bank against the version-21 tree. It covered all three Thai and three English alternatives for every option of all 13 banks, against every question variant and every path into each bank. This round's reply edits:
- Strengths rewritten as plain facts at step3.B/R/W c alt 1, step3.W g alt 1, step4.R c (all three), step4.W c alt 1, step5.B c alt 2, step5.R d alts 0 and 2, and step5.W b alts 1 and 2.

Each new strength is a true fact about its own option: azithromycin is taken once a day; levofloxacin is taken by mouth; a chest X-ray can show an air leak or a pneumonia; ventilation through a tube lowers CO2; a reliever at home is part of most discharge plans; a provincial hospital has a physician team; an ICU team can start ventilation; a senior can help decide on a tube; electrolytes show potassium; a blood count shows the white cell count; and low potassium, which beta-agonists and steroid can cause, can upset the heart rhythm. None of these strengths praises, ranks or grades the choice, and none now speaks more warmly of a reasonable or weaker option than the best options' replies do. The magnesium weigh lines still say why it is not needed here: he is already better, it can lower blood pressure, or the timed gas he needs is missing. The step4.B a replies, on SpO2 88–92% limiting CO2, still fit the new line, and their bold runs quote the option's own label.

Across the whole bank:
- No reply states a wrong fact. Checked closely: macrolide resistance in Thailand, azithromycin and QT, doxycycline photosensitivity, fluoroquinolone restriction and TB masking, beta-lactamase producers against plain amoxicillin, magnesium and blood pressure, potassium with nebulisers and steroid, and NT-proBNP rising with lung strain.

- The safety lines are right for each option: CO2 checks on step2.W d and e; NIV escalation on step4.W a, b and d; sedation and an ICU bed on step4.W c; and active support with ICU at the bedside on step5.W a, b and d.
